ignoredHooks.name: clone_repo_with
ignoredHooks.reason: takes a progress callback, not a fault seam; cloning is none of the three write paths

ignoredHooks.name: identity_with
ignoredHooks.reason: takes an environment lookup to read a commit identity; a read, no durable step

ignoredHooks.name: active_commit_hooks_with
ignoredHooks.reason: takes the policy gate for a read-only probe of git hooks; no durable step

ignoredHooks.name: adopt_with
ignoredHooks.reason: injects the approval and the path prober of a ledger adoption. Per its doc comment the re-anchor record and the audit row are written in one transaction, and a ledger that moved during the probe retries (STALE_PROBE): a race, not a kill between two durable steps. Inferred from the doc comment, not from a test.

boundary.durableBefore: every reflog row and watermark of earlier committed batches; this batch's rows N-1..1 sit only inside its one open write transaction
boundary.notYetWritten: the commit of this batch's rows and of the reflog watermark that names the last of them

injection.detail: a child test process SIGKILLs itself once the batch has inserted GITPULSE_TEST_KILL_AFTER_RECORDED rows (crash_point, compiled only under cfg(all(test, unix))); the test sets it to 6 of 11

rows.recovery: the killed transaction leaves zero rows; the next pass records every entry exactly once, including both identical resets

boundary.durableBefore: every earlier committed batch; this batch's last row is inserted inside the open transaction
boundary.notYetWritten: the watermark upsert and the commit, which follow the last insert

injection.detail: the same crash_point is reachable here: setting GITPULSE_TEST_KILL_AFTER_RECORDED to the number of rows the batch appends kills after the last insert and before the watermark upsert

rows.recovery: expected to match the mid-batch case (rows and watermark share one transaction, so neither survives), but nothing has shown it for this boundary
rows.reason: the hook can reach this boundary but no test sets it to the batch size; the one kill test uses 6 of 11 rows

boundary.durableBefore: an old (writer generation 1) ledger with every row and the old stamp; the migration has added columns and tables inside one immediate transaction
boundary.notYetWritten: the ordinal backfill, the new user_version stamp and the commit

injection.detail: no production hook: the test plants a SQL trigger in the old ledger file that aborts the migration's UPDATE, after the ALTERs have run

rows.recovery: the whole migration rolls back (stamp 1, old shape, no row lost); once the fault is gone the next open completes it

boundary.durableBefore: an old ledger with every row and the old stamp
boundary.notYetWritten: the commit of the one transaction that adds the schema, backfills ordinals and stamps the new generation

injection.detail: a child process opens the ledger and the parent kills it after a 400 ms sleep; no hook pins where the kill lands

rows.recovery: SQLite rolls the open transaction back; the next open migrates from the old stamp
rows.reason: the nearest test kills on a timer and prints, without asserting, the stamp it found, so it never shows the kill landed inside the migration transaction (it can land before the child opens the ledger, or after the commit)

boundary.durableBefore: a transcript pass's events, already committed together with the cursor that names them
boundary.notYetWritten: nothing of this writer: events and cursor share one transaction, so a kill of it cannot split them. The window is the next read finding the cursor lost, stale or behind rows the ledger already holds

injection.detail: not a kill: the same advance is offered twice, and in the second test the cursor row is deleted with forget_transcripts before the same rows are offered again

rows.recovery: rows the ledger already holds are refused by identity, so a re-read after a lost or stale cursor records nothing twice

boundary.durableBefore: the anchor holds the sibling ledger's rows for every page imported so far (1000 rows per page, each page its own transaction) and the initial-pass marker
boundary.notYetWritten: the remaining pages of that sibling, the sibling's import cursor beyond the last page, and the settling of the initial pass

injection.detail: no production hook: the test sets one row's ts_utc to garbage in the sibling ledger so the import fails at the start of page two, mid page two, or the start of page three, then repairs the row

rows.recovery: while the pass is cut short the worktree stays fenced; after repair the next consolidation resumes and the legacy binding resolves

boundary.durableBefore: one sibling ledger fully imported into the anchor, with its cursor
boundary.notYetWritten: the second sibling, whose import fails on its first row

injection.detail: no production hook: the test poisons row 1 of one of two siblings (each order), then repairs it

rows.recovery: after repair both siblings' legacy bindings resolve, whichever sibling failed

boundary.durableBefore: every sibling imported and the initial-pass marker recorded as in progress (source_cursor 0)
boundary.notYetWritten: settle_family_pass, which sets the marker to settled

injection.detail: no hook and no test fails between the last import and the settle

rows.recovery: the pass stays the initial one and resumes next read; sibling rows are judged by birth time, so a post-anchor sibling should still import as history only
rows.reason: the nearest test builds the state of a sibling born after the anchor with no import cursor; it does not cut the pass between the last import and the settle

boundary.durableBefore: the expired backlog, every row still in the ledger
boundary.notYetWritten: the first retention batch: one pass starts no batch, the other has its first batch aborted

injection.detail: one test passes a deadline that already expired so no batch starts; the other plants a BEFORE DELETE trigger that aborts the first batch

rows.recovery: an unfinished pass is not remembered as clean, so the next pass prunes the whole backlog; a failing pass reports its error instead of reading as nothing to prune

boundary.durableBefore: retention batches 1..k of a pass, each its own committed transaction of up to 5000 rows
boundary.notYetWritten: batch k+1 onward, and the memo that the ledger is clean

injection.detail: no hook or test stops a pass after a batch has committed; prune_with_policy loops over prune_events

rows.recovery: expected: each batch is complete on its own and the next pass resumes, since nothing is remembered as clean
rows.reason: the nearest tests stop a pass before any batch commits; none leaves earlier batches committed and cuts the pass after them

boundary.durableBefore: the repository exactly as the agent's git command will find it; no snapshot object, no op ref
boundary.notYetWritten: the pre-operation snapshot (commit object, refs/gitpulse/ops/<n>) and its ledger row

injection.detail: inject_next_op_snapshot_failure_for_test queues a failure that record_op_snapshot_with_limits returns before it takes the lock; serve_op_record turns it into an unsnapshotted ledger row. A second leg of the test uses an unreachable app mailbox

rows.recovery: the failure is never silent: the ledger gets an unsnapshotted row for the command and the hook output carries a visible warning

boundary.durableBefore: the snapshot commit object, written by git commit-tree
boundary.notYetWritten: git update-ref of refs/gitpulse/ops/<n>, so no ref reaches the object

injection.detail: no hook between commit-tree and update-ref in record_op_snapshot_with_limits

rows.recovery: expected: an unreachable object that git gc collects, and the next snapshot reuses the same sequence number
rows.reason: no injection point exists between the object write and the ref write

boundary.durableBefore: refs/gitpulse/ops/<n> written by a compare-and-set update-ref
boundary.notYetWritten: retention pruning (expiry and over-cap eviction), which can fail and is propagated with ?

injection.detail: no hook makes the prune fail or kills between update-ref and the prune

rows.recovery: unknown: a prune error after the ref exists makes record_op_snapshot return Err, so serve_op_record writes an unsnapshotted row for a snapshot that does exist
rows.reason: the only prune test is the success path; no test fails the prune after the ref is written, and the code appears to report that as unsnapshotted

boundary.durableBefore: the snapshot ref and its retention pass
boundary.notYetWritten: the ledger row for the snapshot (record_op_snapshot_event, best effort: it returns an Option and the caller ignores it)

injection.detail: no hook between the prune and the ledger append

rows.recovery: expected: a snapshot ref with no ledger row; list_op_snapshots still finds it because it reads refs, not the ledger
rows.reason: no injection point, and no test makes the ledger append fail after the ref is written

boundary.durableBefore: every recorded ref restored by one atomic update-ref --stdin transaction
boundary.notYetWritten: the move of HEAD to the recorded symbolic ref or detached oid

injection.detail: no hook between the update-ref transaction and the HEAD update in undo_op_snapshot_with_gate

rows.recovery: unknown: refs are restored while HEAD still names the old branch; a second undo would find the refs equal to the snapshot, not to the plan
rows.reason: the nearest test covers the refusals before any write and the full success path, never a stop between the ref restore and the HEAD move

boundary.durableBefore: refs restored and HEAD moved to the snapshot's branch or commit
boundary.notYetWritten: git read-tree --reset -u HEAD, which brings the index and working tree to the restored HEAD

injection.detail: no hook between the HEAD update and read-tree

rows.recovery: unknown: HEAD and refs match the snapshot while the index and files still hold the pre-undo state, which would read as local modifications
rows.reason: no injection point and no test stops or fails the read-tree

boundary.durableBefore: refs, HEAD, index and working tree restored
boundary.notYetWritten: the git.op.undo ledger row with before_ref and after_ref (record_op_undo_event)

injection.detail: no hook between read-tree and the ledger append

rows.recovery: expected: the undo happened and the ledger has no row for it
rows.reason: no injection point, and no test makes the ledger append fail after the restore

boundary.durableBefore: the merged tree and the squash or merge commit objects (merge-tree --write-tree, commit-tree); source branch, target ref and worktree untouched
boundary.notYetWritten: the move of the target branch (ff-only merge in its checkout, or update-ref with a compare-and-set)

injection.detail: merge_worktree_pipeline, the engine behind the gitpulse_worktree_merge MCP tool, takes no seam and has no hook

rows.recovery: expected: unreachable objects only; a rerun builds the merge again
rows.reason: no injection point in the pipeline; the nearest test runs it to completion or to a refusal and never stops it between steps

boundary.durableBefore: the target branch moved to the merge or squash commit
boundary.notYetWritten: removal of the source worktree, deletion of the source branch and release of its lane claim

injection.detail: no seam between the target move and the cleanup block in merge_worktree_pipeline

rows.recovery: unknown: a rerun depends on verify_branch_integration reporting the source as already integrated (for a squash, content-equal rather than an ancestor) and then only doing cleanup
rows.reason: no injection point in the pipeline and no test reruns it over a target that already holds the merge; the desktop teardown engine has such a test, this one does not

boundary.durableBefore: the source worktree removed (renamed aside, record removed, files deleted)
boundary.notYetWritten: git branch -d or -D of the source branch

injection.detail: no seam between remove_worktree and the branch delete in merge_worktree_pipeline

rows.recovery: expected: a merged branch with no worktree remains; rerun finds the branch integrated and deletes it
rows.reason: no injection point and no test in the pipeline for this boundary

boundary.durableBefore: worktree removed and branch deleted
boundary.notYetWritten: agent_bus::release_lanes_matching, which drops the lane claims that name the worktree or branch

injection.detail: no seam before the lane release in merge_worktree_pipeline

rows.recovery: unknown: a claim for a lane whose worktree and branch are gone stays registered, and a rerun finds no source branch to clean up
rows.reason: no injection point, no test, and a rerun has no branch left that would trigger the release

boundary.durableBefore: a gitpulse-quarantine-* directory under the temp directory, holding the objects of the conflict check
boundary.notYetWritten: its removal by the owner's Drop guard, which a SIGKILL never runs

injection.detail: the test plants aged and fresh quarantine-named directories and runs the sweep; it does not kill a merge

rows.recovery: the next ObjectQuarantine::new sweeps directories older than an hour, bounded per sweep, and follows no symlink

boundary.durableBefore: the lane's work merged into the target (fast-forward, or a squash commit made by hand)
boundary.notYetWritten: worktree removal and branch delete of the desktop merge-and-teardown engine (merge_and_teardown_configured)

injection.detail: the test performs the merge itself with git (merge --ff-only, or merge --squash plus commit), then calls the teardown as the recovery call would

rows.recovery: the next call reports merged, removes the worktree and deletes the branch; the squash case may instead refuse cleanly, but never leaves a half state (the squash test accepts either)

boundary.durableBefore: a git merge started in the target checkout and stopped on a conflict (MERGE_HEAD present)
boundary.notYetWritten: the conclusion of that merge, and the teardown

injection.detail: the test runs a conflicting git merge in the target checkout and leaves it parked

rows.recovery: the next teardown is refused, MERGE_HEAD and the conflicted file are left exactly as they were

boundary.durableBefore: the worktree directory renamed into the teardown holding directory
boundary.notYetWritten: removal of git's worktree record (and, when that step fails, the put-back rename)

injection.detail: the test renames the directory by hand and calls again; a second test passes try_rename_aside_with a record-removal step that fails after the record is gone and a put-back that fails

rows.recovery: the stale record is cleared by the next removal or prune, the aside is swept; files whose put-back failed are held back from the sweep and named in the error

boundary.durableBefore: git no longer lists the worktree; its files sit in the holding directory (whole, or half deleted)
boundary.notYetWritten: the deletion of those files

injection.detail: the tests prune the record by hand, or plant a partly deleted aside, then run the sweep

rows.recovery: the next teardown's sweep deletes the aside, a partial tree included

boundary.durableBefore: the lane merged, its record gone, its branch deleted, its files in the holding directory
boundary.notYetWritten: the deletion of the files, which fails

injection.detail: the closure passed as delete_aside returns an error, through merge_and_teardown_with_seams and remove_worktree_with

rows.recovery: the merge still reports merged, the cleanup error names the aside path, and the next removal sweeps it

boundary.durableBefore: the lane merged and its worktree removed
boundary.notYetWritten: deletion of the source branch, refused by the policy gate

injection.detail: the gate closure passed to merge_and_teardown_worktree refuses git branch; this is a policy refusal, not a hook symbol

rows.recovery: the call is Ok with worktree_removed true, branch_deleted false and the gate's reason in branch_error

boundary.durableBefore: the lane's work merged into the target
boundary.notYetWritten: removal of the worktree, which fails on every bounded retry (a locked lane), and so the branch delete

injection.detail: a locked worktree makes every removal attempt fail; merge_and_teardown_with takes the sleep closure so the retries are counted instead of waited

rows.recovery: the call is Ok with merged true, the removal error and branch error set, the worktree and branch kept, after exactly the bounded retries

boundary.durableBefore: the moved-aside files, being deleted while another sweep deletes the same tree
boundary.notYetWritten: the end of the delete, because children vanish under the walk

injection.detail: delete_dir_tree_with takes the single-pass remover, which the tests make report NotFound once, or on every pass

rows.recovery: a vanished tree counts as deleted; a walk that keeps vanishing is retried a bounded number of times and then returned as an error with the aside kept

boundary.durableBefore: the target ref moved to the candidate by compare-and-set, and zero or more checkouts holding the target already advanced by read-tree
boundary.notYetWritten: the remaining checkouts' index and files, which fail to follow

injection.detail: the gate closure fails the read-tree, or edits the checkouts when update-index is judged; a failed step, not a kill. The tests assert the injection point was reached

rows.recovery: the ref and every advanced checkout are put back (a ref another actor moved is left alone), HEAD, index and files match what the person left, and a restore that cannot finish says which checkout to inspect

boundary.durableBefore: refs/heads/<target> moved to the candidate
boundary.notYetWritten: read-tree in each checkout that holds the target, so HEAD names the new commit while index and files still hold the old tree

injection.detail: restore_after_failed_advance runs only when the advance returns an error; a process that dies between update-ref and read-tree runs nothing

rows.recovery: unknown: the checkout would show the merge's changes as local modifications, and nothing records that a landing was cut short
rows.reason: the nearest tests fail the step and let the restore run; no hook or test kills the process between the ref move and the checkout advance

boundary.durableBefore: a detached scratch worktree gitpulse-candidate-<pid>-<n> under the temp directory, registered with git, while the candidate is verified outside the lock
boundary.notYetWritten: its removal, and the landing of the candidate

injection.detail: verify_in_scratch takes the verifier as a closure but nothing kills the process while it runs

rows.recovery: unknown: a search for gitpulse-candidate finds only the creation site and two tests that no scratch is left after a normal run; no sweep of a scratch left by a dead process
rows.reason: no injection point, and no code or test that sweeps a scratch worktree a killed process left behind

boundary.durableBefore: the merge landed on the target
boundary.notYetWritten: the removal of the worktree and the deletion of the branch, which re-read the lane and refuse if a file appeared or the branch moved after the merge was checked

injection.detail: no seam between the landing and the unchanged_since_merge re-check

rows.recovery: by the code: the merge stands, the worktree and branch are kept and the reason is reported; no test shows it
rows.reason: no test asserts either of the two refusals (a search of the sources finds their text only in worktree.rs)

boundary.durableBefore: merge landed, worktree removed, branch deleted
boundary.notYetWritten: the repository's post_merge hook, which exits non-zero

injection.detail: the repository's gitpulse config declares a post_merge command that exits 4

rows.recovery: the call stays Ok with the teardown complete, and hook_error carries the hook's output
